title: Render social export images in the browser from server-computed crop geometry
context: Issue #10 needed real 1:1/4:5/9:16/16:9 crops, a cover title and exact pixel sizes in the export manifest. The demo has no server image pipeline or object storage; images are bundled fixtures (photos 1086x1448, SVGs 600x800 viewBox). Saved workspaces live as JSON in Postgres with schema_version 1.
decision: The server (MockStudio.export) computes every crop rectangle and exact output size with a pure exportFrame() in packages/contracts; the browser draws the JPEGs on a canvas from that manifest (apps/web/src/lib/social-render.ts). The preview uses the same geometry (object-fit cover + object-position = focus) and container-unit text sizes. Older saved workspaces are upgraded on restore (default pack, focus, fixture sizes) instead of a schema migration.
consequences: Manifest sizes are exact by construction; e2e checks JPEG headers against them.
Export needs a browser with canvas, roundRect and container units.
A future server renderer must reuse exportFrame so sizes stay identical.
alternatives_rejected: Server-side rendering with sharp/canvas in a route: adds a native dependency and CPU work on Vercel for a mock demo; deferred to the real export renderer.
Recording crop settings only and shipping originals: fails the 'actual dimensions' acceptance criterion.
Bumping schema_version with a SQL migration: the change is additive, and the current store returns 503 for any other version, which would lock out existing sessions.
